title: Ngā Whetū o te Tau Hou | The Stars of the New Year
location: Te Whatu Stardome | Observatory & Planetarium, 670 Manukau Rd, Maungakiekie/One Tree Hill Domain, Epsom, Auckland 1023, Auckland
description:
In this immersive planetarium experience, you’ll journey through the night sky to explore the Matariki star cluster and its importance in Aotearoa and te ao Māori.
Discover the rich pūrākau (stories), science and traditions connected to each of the nine whetū, learn about the Maramataka (the Māori lunar calendar), and reflect on how Matariki guides us through the cycles of the year along with many other significant stars.
Whether you’re reconnecting with Matariki or experiencing it for the first time, this show is a great way to honour the season and gain a deeper appreciation of Māori astronomy and our place within the cosmos.
Keywords: Nga Whetu o te Tau Hou The Stars of the New Year

title: OWASP New Zealand - Auckland Meetup
description:
Join us for the next **OWASP New Zealand Chapter** meetup! We are gathering the local application security community for an evening of technical talks, networking, and knowledge sharing.

* **When:** Tuesday, 14th July 2026
* **Where:** **Lightspeed Office** 2 Nuffield Street, Newmarket, Auckland 1023, New Zealand
* **Time:** 5:30 PM (Doors open for networking), 6:00 PM (Presentations begin)

We present an introductory talk about the OWASP Top 10 (2025 edition) with a new item each meeting. With the new edition OWASP Top 10, we're starting at A01:2025 Broken Access Control.

**Thanks to Our Host**
A big thank you to [Lightspeed](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/au/) for sponsoring the venue and catering and for supporting the local security community.

**Agenda**

* 6:00 PM OWASP Introduction, Top 10
* 6:30 PM Break
* 6:45 PM Technical Talk

**Technical Topic Speaker: Ricky Gummadi**
Ricky Gummadi is a Senior Solution Architect at Microsoft, based in Auckland, focused on AI, cloud architecture, and developer platforms. He works closely with enterprise customers across New Zealand to design and implement production-ready AI systems. Ricky is also part of the core development team contributing to the Agent Governance Toolkit, with a focus on enabling safe, reliable, and governed agentic AI workloads.
**Talk Title: Agentic AI Governance**
As AI systems evolve from assistants to autonomous agents, the focus shifts from what the model says to what the system actually does. This talk introduces the Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT), a framework for bringing deterministic, runtime governance to agentic systems. We’ll explore why prompt-based safety is not sufficient for production scenarios, walk through the OWASP Agentic Top 10 risks, and look at how policies, identity, sandboxing, and observability can be applied to mitigate these risks in real-world architectures.

title: Power BI & Fabric Updates & Lightning Talks [In Person]
location: Level 5, 22 Viaduct Harbour Ave Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
This month we are going to have two short lightning talks about Power BI and Fabric, and also a review of the most important updates recently on the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric, and the AI-related topics about it. Join us for this session of learning and networking.

**Agenda:**
5:00-5:30 PM Welcome and Networking/Refreshments
5:30-6:00 PM A review of the Power BI and Fabric Updates - Reza Rad
6:00-7:00 PM Two Lightning talk sessions
7:00-7:30 PM Wrap Up

**Topic 1:** **Native Power BI Visuals, Reimagined: Small Tweaks, Big Impact**

####

Many developers assume native Power BI visuals are too rigid for high-end reporting. They often reach out to use custom visuals that add unnecessary complexity.
This session challenges that "limit" of native Power BI visuals by demonstrating how intentional, creative configuration can unlock hidden potential within the standard toolkit.
Through live examples, you will see how you can move from "standard" to "standout," experience.

**Topic 2:** **Lessons learnt: Handling Incremental Parquet Files in Microsoft Fabric**

What happens when an upstream CDC process drops incremental Parquet files into OneLake every 15 minutes for 536 tables across 14 schemas? You build a Fabric pipeline that can't afford to fall behind.
In this session, I ’ll break down a battle-tested Fabric architecture designed for high-frequency ingestion. I will also cover the metadata-driven configuration table that prioritises high volume schemas, the specific Spark tuning required to hit a 15-minute SLA, and the append/merge logic used to build clean Delta tables.
Finally, I will be sharing honest insights into Fabric capacity consumption, error handling strategies, and the critical design mistakes we made so that you don't have to.

**Speakers:**

* Medha Bandari
* Shruthi Simha Chippagiri

title: Less Grind, More Ship: AI-Powered Development in Practice
description:
This session looks at how AI is reshaping every stage of the development process itself – from the programming paradigms, to the PRD specification processes, to the way we manage multiple innovative projects at once.

The focus is practical and aimed at AI developers, project managers, product owners, and tech architects - anyone writing software or managing projects with AI will find something useful.

We'll explore-

* The current cutting edge in AI dev processes, specifically circuit/loop engineering approaches
* Desired state methodologies in AI development
* New concepts for better project management and better results
* Strategies for concurrent development
* New ideation processes leveraging AI to generate novel solutions and approaches
* Where new techniques offer breakthrough performance vs. where they add unnecessary complexity
* Practical workflows and tools that are actually worth integrating

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Governing AI in the Enterprise: Purview, Copilot Security & Data Protection
description:
Microsoft Copilot and enterprise AI adoption are accelerating — but most organisations are deploying AI faster than their governance, data protection, and security controls can keep up with.

IT Pros and Security Architects are now on the hook for managing AI-related data exposure, permission sprawl, and compliance gaps — often without a clear framework.

In this session, we cut through the hype and focus on what controls actually matter, with live demos showing how Microsoft Purview, Entra ID, and Defender work together to govern AI safely.

**Susantha Silva** is a Senior Cloud Security Solutions Architect with over 18 years of Microsoft security expertise, operating across the APAC and MEA regions from his base in Auckland, New Zealand.

He specialises in helping enterprises design, assess, and strengthen their cloud security posture through Microsoft-native technologies.

title: LIVE Day: Weather Science
location: MOTAT, 805 Great North Road and 98 Motions Road, Western Springs, Auckland, Auckland
description:
LIVE Days are interactive and hands-on days filled with learning, play and special moments, perfect for the whole whānau!
With live entertainment, collection items, plus plenty of activities - there's a little something for everyone.
This July at LIVE DAY: Weather Science uncover the stories of the weather-related stars in the Matariki cluster, Waipunarangi and Ururangi.
Waipunarangi is associated with the various forms of rain that we experience throughout the year as it falls from the sky and washes over the earth, nourishing all living things. If you can’t see Waipunarangi clearly during Matariki, the year will bring lots of rain and maybe some flooding. If she’s bright and clear, the rain will be light.
Ururangi connects us to the different winds and this whetū determines the nature of these winds. If Ururangi is hard to see when the cluster of Matariki rises, the year will be windy. If he is bright and clear, the winds will be calm.
Make and take home your own cloud finder, have fun with weather science experiments featuring raindrops and rainbows, and find out more about the different winds and how they work at our latest exhibition Ngā hau a Tāwhirirangi Forces of Flight, in the Aviation Hall.
Included in General Admission.
We recommend parking outside the Aviation Hall and enjoying the free heritage tram ride between sites.

description:
Bring your whānau and join Restore Hibiscus & Bays and Te Herenga Waka o Orewa for a special Matariki planting day!
Together we’ll be planting native plants to help restore the marae grounds, riverbank and awa, continuing the regular restoration mahi already underway at this special site.
Matariki is a time to remember the past, celebrate the present and look to the future. This community planting day is a chance to come together, care for the whenua and help create a healthier, more resilient environment for future generations.
Everyone is welcome and no experience is needed. Tools and guidance will be provided, along with morning tea and hot drinks.
On the day there will also a fantastic opportunity to learn more about water monitoring of the awa.
What to bring:

gardening gloves
water bottle
snacks
sturdy shoes or boots
clothing suitable for the weather
a clean spade if you have one.

Come along, bring your whānau, and be part of this special Matariki planting day. Every plant in the ground helps care for the awa, the whenua and the future.
